title: What Comes at Dusk
logline: As the light goes at the edge of a village, a ritual specialist and a family build an offering stand for a sick relative, and the whole village stays up with them until dawn.

object.note: Object 8 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From a rite for someone gone to a night-long rite for someone still here: a village staying up with a family and a ritual specialist for a sick relative.

thread_out.thread: What a community gives one of its own becomes what is owed on paper: a village shop's credit book, where some debts are struck through when the debtor dies.

lesson.in_simple_terms: The texts picture many kinds of life we cannot see, and they teach that how a life begins and what it meets along the way can come from different causes. Where someone starts is never the whole story.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: අපට නොපෙනෙන බොහෝ ආකාරයේ ජීවිත ගැන ග්‍රන්ථ කියන අතර, ජීවිතයක ආරම්භයත් එහි ගමනේදී ලැබෙන සැප දුකත් වෙනස් හේතුවලින් ඇතිවිය හැකි බැවින් කෙනෙකු ආරම්භ කළ තැන ඔවුන්ගේ මුළු කතාව නොවන බව ද ඒවා උගන්වයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma calls the joining of one life's last moment to the next life's first moment, with no gap between them, rebirth-linking (paṭisandhi), and it names four kinds. The Pradeepika notes that the kind of birth a being has and the comfort or hardship it meets during life can come from different actions, so a hard beginning does not fix everything that follows. The texts also place many unseen beings on their map of existence, say that for animals and unhappy spirits the 'plane' is simply the kind of life they are living rather than a place, and say that no being stays in a hard state once the force that put it there is used up.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Offering stands are built at dusk, masks and drums are readied, and offerings are set at the village's edge while the whole community stays awake with one family until dawn. The film watches the rite without saying what the unseen beings it addresses are. What the viewer notices is that one sick person's night is held by many hands, not reduced to a single cause.

key_terms.en: rebirth-linking; the first consciousness of a new existence

lesson.caution: It does not mean anyone's illness says something about their past, or that the film confirms which beings the ritual addresses; the texts' categories of birth must never be applied to real people.
lesson.builds_on: From a rite for someone who has gone, this film turns to someone still alive and in trouble, and adds that where a life starts and what it meets on the way have different causes.
